## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhidura Sutta* (Iti 77; It 3.28; PTS It 69) is a discourse found in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Its core teaching addresses the impermanence and fragility of conditioned phenomena: the Buddha teaches that the material body is fragile and falls apart, consciousness is subject to fading or cessation, and all acquisitions (*upadhi*) are inconstant, painful, and subject to change [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations include an English rendering titled *Fragile* by Bhikkhu Sujato, among eighteen translations preserved in sixteen languages on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Regarding textual parallels and reuse, SuttaCentral lists no direct external parallels for the discourse [SuttaCentral]. The automated alignment tools of DharmaNexus identify internal Pali text reuse spanning 34 matches across ten other discourses within the *Itivuttaka* [DharmaNexus]. These matches predominantly represent shared introductory and formulaic prose segments (such as segment ranges §0.1–3.1 and §0.1–2.1), shared with texts including the *Duccarita Sutta* (Iti 64), *Soceyya Sutta* (Iti 66), *Moneyya Sutta* (Iti 67), and *Puññakiriyavatthu Sutta* (Iti 60) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are registered by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
